To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we (1) propose a new algorithm for detecting logical sessions, which improves the state-of-the art in both online and offline scenarios; (2) show that logical sessions are a good proxy for search missions, but that search mission detection still is a challenging task; (3) introduce a new corpus of 880 queries, labeled with logical sessions and search missions; (4) show that the new algorithm outperforms the state-of-theart in the online scenario; (5) show that the

(1) search missions are more common than logical search sessions, (2) search missions are often hierarchical, and (3), the search history of a user often contains multiple missions, which are interleaved with each other

(1) the cascading method can be improved by exploiting Linked Open Datasets to better detect logical sessions and (2) search engines can benefit from knowledge about search missions to better support users
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of information needs and search missions, which is a necessary prerequisite for the development of search support systems.
the question: how can we better understand the dialog and the user’s search behavior?
the question of how search engines can better support users by incorporating search mission knowledge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the new approach is able to improve session detection and thus to provide a solid basis for search mission detection, which is the first step toward a more detailed understanding of user search behavior and thus a more effective support for the user.
the search engine community should move away from the session paradigm towards search missions.
the new algorithm for logical search session detection, as well as our new search mission detection approach are promising and can be applied to real-world data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a new approach to search mission detection that is more accurate than the state-of-the- art, which is based on cascading methods, while at the same time being applicable to the online scenario.
we provide a better understanding of search missions and how they are related to physical and logical sessions, and we offer a new algorithm for detecting logical sessions and search missions.
we propose a method for search mission detection that is applicable to real-world scenarios and that we provide a new corpus that enables further research in this area.
The main takeaway from our work is that
search missions can provide a better understanding of users’ behavior and thus can be a valuable asset for search engines to better serve users.
search missions are an important concept to understand user behavior.
the detection of search missions is a promising step toward a better understanding of user behavior and the dialog between user, search engine, and the web.
